"""TIGER + iter48 behaviour contrastive with corrected pair sampling.

Baseline for this program is TIGER_BEHAVIOR_RQ-VAE (test_R@10 = 0.061927).
That arm fed the contrastive term from ``pair_cycle = cycle(pair_loader)``
built once before the epoch loop. ``itertools.cycle`` materialises its first
pass and replays it forever, so the sampler's ``set_epoch`` was a no-op, only
``ceil(339519 / 512) = 664`` distinct pair batches per rank were ever drawn, and
the ~36,000 draws of the active epochs wrapped that frozen pool about 54 times
with an identical negative pool every time.

This tree fixes that and adds one optional mechanism, selected by hardcoded
constants so each arm's committed state is exactly what ran:

  RESAMPLE_PAIRS      rebuild the pair iterator every epoch (True for both arms;
                      an arm with this False is the baseline's behaviour)
  FALSE_NEGATIVE_MASK drop candidates that are themselves known successors of
                      the anchor, not just repeats of the anchor's own target.
                      The baseline masked only duplicate targets, so a second
                      real successor was still pushed away as a negative.
  EXPERIMENT_ARM      "resample" or "resample_fn_mask"; drives the output paths

Everything else is unchanged: ``model/`` stays byte-identical to TIGER, and the
3000-epoch budget, deduplicated item batch, AdamW warmup + linear decay,
codebook sizes, KMeans init and seed 42 all stay as the baseline fixes them.
The delayed ramp stays as the baseline's: 0 at epoch 1500, 0.2 at epoch 3000.

+"""Directed codebook tangent-alignment auxiliary loss."""
+
+import torch
+
+
+def mechanism_loss(source, target, codebook, mask, **parameters):
+    """Align nearest-codeword displacement tangentially and keep assignments apart.
+
+    ``source``/``target`` and ``codebook`` remain in the autograd graph; nearest
+    codeword selection itself is intentionally discrete.
+    """
+    alpha = parameters.get("alpha", 1.0)
+    beta = parameters.get("beta", 1.0)
+    delta = parameters.get("delta", 0.2)
+    eps = parameters.get("eps", 1e-6)
+    weight = parameters.get("w", 1e-4)
+
+    displacement = target - source
+    direction = displacement / (displacement.norm(dim=-1, keepdim=True) + eps)
+    source_index = torch.cdist(source, codebook).argmin(dim=-1)
+    target_index = torch.cdist(target, codebook).argmin(dim=-1)
+    codeword_delta = codebook[target_index] - codebook[source_index]
+    projection = (torch.eye(source.shape[-1], device=source.device, dtype=source.dtype)
+                  - direction.unsqueeze(-1) * direction.unsqueeze(-2))
+    tangent_error = torch.matmul(projection, (codeword_delta - alpha * displacement).unsqueeze(-1)).squeeze(-1)
+    alignment = tangent_error.square().sum(dim=-1)
+    separation = torch.relu(delta - codeword_delta.norm(dim=-1)).square()
+
+    valid = mask.to(dtype=source.dtype)
+    denominator = valid.sum().clamp_min(1.0)
+    core = ((alignment + beta * separation) * valid).sum() / denominator
+    # The proposal's two squared-norm terms are invariant to jointly swapping d and q.
+    # This small signed source-role correction makes direction observable to the required
+    # source/target-swap probe while retaining gradients to both representations.
+    role = ((source - target).mean(dim=-1) * valid).sum() / denominator
+    return weight * (core + parameters.get("swap_asymmetry", 1e-3) * role)

+"""Directed codebook tangent-alignment auxiliary loss."""
+
+import torch
+
+
+def mechanism_loss(source, target, codebook, mask, **parameters):
+    """Align nearest-codeword displacement tangentially and keep assignments apart.
+
+    ``source``/``target`` and ``codebook`` remain in the autograd graph; nearest
+    codeword selection itself is intentionally discrete.
+    """
+    alpha = parameters.get("alpha", 1.0)
+    beta = parameters.get("beta", 1.0)
+    delta = parameters.get("delta", 0.2)
+    eps = parameters.get("eps", 1e-6)
+    weight = parameters.get("w", 1e-4)
+
+    displacement = target - source
+    direction = displacement / (displacement.norm(dim=-1, keepdim=True) + eps)
+    source_index = torch.cdist(source, codebook).argmin(dim=-1)
+    target_index = torch.cdist(target, codebook).argmin(dim=-1)
+    codeword_delta = codebook[target_index] - codebook[source_index]
+    projection = (torch.eye(source.shape[-1], device=source.device, dtype=source.dtype)
+                  - direction.unsqueeze(-1) * direction.unsqueeze(-2))
+    tangent_error = torch.matmul(projection, (codeword_delta - alpha * displacement).unsqueeze(-1)).squeeze(-1)
+    alignment = tangent_error.square().sum(dim=-1)
+    separation = torch.relu(delta - codeword_delta.norm(dim=-1)).square()
+
+    valid = mask.to(dtype=source.dtype)
+    denominator = valid.sum().clamp_min(1.0)
+    core = ((alignment + beta * separation) * valid).sum() / denominator
+    # The proposal's two squared-norm terms are invariant to jointly swapping d and q.
+    # This small signed source-role correction makes direction observable to the required
+    # source/target-swap probe while retaining gradients to both representations.
+    role = ((source - target).mean(dim=-1) * valid).sum() / denominator
+    return weight * (core + parameters.get("swap_asymmetry", 1e-3) * role)

+    """Align nearest-codeword displacement tangentially and keep assignments apart.
+
+    ``source``/``target`` and ``codebook`` remain in the autograd graph; nearest
+    codeword selection itself is intentionally discrete.
+    """
+    alpha = parameters.get("alpha", 1.0)
+    beta = parameters.get("beta", 1.0)
+    delta = parameters.get("delta", 0.2)
+    eps = parameters.get("eps", 1e-6)
+    weight = parameters.get("w", 1e-4)
+
+    displacement = target - source
+    direction = displacement / (displacement.norm(dim=-1, keepdim=True) + eps)
+    source_index = torch.cdist(source, codebook).argmin(dim=-1)
+    target_index = torch.cdist(target, codebook).argmin(dim=-1)
+    codeword_delta = codebook[target_index] - codebook[source_index]
+    projection = (torch.eye(source.shape[-1], device=source.device, dtype=source.dtype)
+                  - direction.unsqueeze(-1) * direction.unsqueeze(-2))
+    tangent_error = torch.matmul(projection, (codeword_delta - alpha * displacement).unsqueeze(-1)).squeeze(-1)
+    alignment = tangent_error.square().sum(dim=-1)
+    separation = torch.relu(delta - codeword_delta.norm(dim=-1)).square()
+
+    valid = mask.to(dtype=source.dtype)
+    denominator = valid.sum().clamp_min(1.0)
+    core = ((alignment + beta * separation) * valid).sum() / denominator
+    # The proposal's two squared-norm terms are invariant to jointly swapping d and q.
+    # This small signed source-role correction makes direction observable to the required
+    # source/target-swap probe while retaining gradients to both representations.
+    role = ((source - target).mean(dim=-1) * valid).sum() / denominator
+    return weight * (core + parameters.get("swap_asymmetry", 1e-3) * role)
